title: Clearing malfunctions
subtitle: Tap, Rack, Assess, the stove-pipe jam and failure to go into battery

lines: In this episode, we practise clearing malfunctions on a semi-automatic pistol.
In your practical assessment, you will be required to identify and rectify malfunctions.

scenes.definition: Also known as an immediate action drill. A drill designed to rectify several different problems that could have caused a malfunction.
lines: A malfunction drill is also known as an immediate action drill.
It is a drill designed to rectify several different problems that could have caused a malfunction.
You need to practise this drill often, with dummy ammunition, in your own firearm.

scenes.heading: Failure to fire: Tap, Rack, Assess
bullets: Tap the magazine firmly at the bottom
Rack the slide: pull it back and let it go
lines: When you squeeze the trigger and experience a failure to fire, you do three things.

lines.text: One: tap the magazine firmly at the bottom.

lines: This will ensure that the magazine is properly seated, and that the ammunition is being pushed up properly by the magazine spring and follower.

lines.text: Two: rack the slide, which means pull back the slide and let it go.

lines: This will eject the faulty cartridge, and load a new cartridge into the chamber.

lines.text: Three: assess your target once again, to see if the target requires another shot.

lines: This drill is simply known as Tap, Rack, Assess.

scenes.caption: Immediate action drill for a misfire, photos 1 to 3
lines: Here is the immediate action drill for a misfire, in the book's photos.
In photo one, the shooter is in the normal firing position, and has experienced a malfunction.
Two: pull the firearm closer to your body, where you have more control over it.
Three: place your left hand under the magazine, ready to give a firm tap to the bottom of the magazine.

scenes.caption: Photos 4 to 6: Tap, Rack, let the slide go
lines: Four: tap, making sure the magazine is seated in the magazine-well.
Five: rack, pulling back the slide to eject the faulty cartridge.
Six: let the slide go, and make sure that you maintain control over the muzzle of the firearm.

scenes.caption: Photos 7 and 8: Assess, re-engage
lines: Seven: assess, checking that your firearm has been cleared.
Eight: re-engage your target.

scenes.heading: If Tap, Rack, Assess does not fix it

lines.text: If for some reason the Tap, Rack, Assess drill does not fix your problem, remove the magazine.
Work the slide to clear the malfunction.
Cycle the slide once more to chamber a new cartridge.
The gun should now be ready for firing once again.

scenes.caption: Stove-pipe jam: empty case lodged in the ejection port
lines: Now, the stove-pipe jam, caused when the empty case fails to eject completely from the firearm.
Here you can see the empty case protruding from the ejection port of the pistol.

scenes.caption: Clearing a stove-pipe jam, photos 2 and 3
lines: Bring the firearm closer to your body, making sure your finger is off the trigger.
The left hand now gets ready to sweep the case out of the ejection port.
Sweep the hand back, controlling the muzzle of the firearm, and with your finger off the trigger.

scenes.caption: Stove-pipe jam, photo 4: ready to fire again
lines: Four: the gun is now ready to be fired once again.

scenes.caption: After firing, the slide has failed to go into battery
lines: Next, failure to go into battery.
This means the slide has not moved all the way forward, and has therefore not properly chambered the cartridge.
In the photograph, the slide is not properly forward on the firearm.

scenes.caption: Safe direction, finger off the trigger, then Tap
lines: Keep the firearm in a safe direction, with your finger off the trigger.
Tap, making sure the magazine is seated in the magazine-well.

scenes.caption: Rack with the ejection port facing downwards, then release
lines: Rack, pulling back the slide to eject the faulty cartridge.
Tilt the firearm so that the ejection port is facing downwards, and the force of gravity will expel the cartridge.
Release the slide.
The gun is now ready to be fired once again.

scenes.question: Your pistol fails to fire. What is the immediate action drill?
lines: You squeeze the trigger, and experience a failure to fire.
What is the immediate action drill?
reveal: Tap the magazine firmly at the bottom, rack the slide, and assess your target once again.

scenes.question: Clearing a failure to go into battery, which way should the ejection port face as you rack?
lines: When you rack to clear a failure to go into battery, which way should the ejection port face?
reveal: Tilt the firearm so the ejection port faces downwards, and the force of gravity will expel the cartridge.

points: Failure to fire: Tap, Rack, Assess
Not fixed: magazine out, clear, re-insert, cycle
Stove-pipe: sweep the case out of the port
Out of battery: tap, rack with the port down
Finger off the trigger, control the muzzle
lines: So, for a failure to fire: Tap, Rack, Assess.
If that doesn't fix it, remove the magazine, clear the malfunction, re-insert the magazine, and cycle the slide.
For a stove-pipe jam, sweep the case out of the ejection port.
For a failure to go into battery, tap, then rack with the ejection port facing downwards.
And throughout, keep your finger off the trigger, and control the muzzle.
